citeAs: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen (2023). MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv:2311.16502.
creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen (IN.AI Research, University of Waterloo, The Ohio State University, Carnegie Mellon University, University of Victoria, Princeton University)
description: MMMU (Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning) is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines (Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering) across 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 highly heterogeneous image types such as charts, diagrams, maps, tables, music sheets, and chemical structures.
name: MMMU
rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students (including co-authors) specializing in the relevant academic majors across 30 subjects. For human expert evaluation, 90 college senior students were selected to represent a wide range of experts in the corresponding 30 subjects (3 student experts per subject).
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A secondary review team rigorously vetted annotations for quality and guideline adherence. Regular audits of random samples from the dataset were conducted to ensure sustained quality and consistency. Ambiguities or unclear data instances were flagged for detailed review and collaboratively examined in team meetings.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom web interface developed for data annotation and verification (developed by Tianyu Zheng as part of the project)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators (over 50 university students specializing in the relevant majors) collected questions from free online resources, quizzes, and textbooks, strictly adhering to copyright and licensing regulations. All questions must contain one or more images, be written in English, meet college-level difficulty, and not be ambiguous. Each question was annotated with: question type (multiple-choice or open-ended), question text, answer options, correct answer, image types, question difficulty, and explanation (if available). Questions were stored in JSON format. Annotators were advised to select questions without immediately available answers to reduce data contamination risk.
rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases. The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. Subjects like law and linguistics were excluded because it was difficult to find enough relevant multimodal problems. Annotators were advised to select questions without immediately available answers to reduce data contamination concerns with foundation models. The benchmark is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI as there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and "90th percentile of skilled adults."
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected in three stages. First, 30 subjects from six disciplines were selected based on the principle that visual inputs should be commonly adopted. Second, over 50 university students (including co-authors) specializing in these majors were recruited as annotators to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks, online resources, and lecture materials, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. Annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations and to select questions without immediately available answers (e.g., answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks). This process resulted in a diverse collection of approximately 13K questions.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multimodal questions collected from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, online resources, and lecture materials. The raw collection comprised approximately 13K questions before quality filtering. Questions include images of diverse types (diagrams, charts, photographs, chemical structures, music sheets, medical images, etc.) interleaved with text.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Web Scraping
rai:dataLimitations: MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI, as per the definition, because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and "90th percentile of skilled adults," nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle. The manual curation process may carry biases. The focus on college-level subjects might not cover all aspects needed for Expert AGI evaluation. Some subjects (e.g., law and linguistics) were excluded due to difficulty finding enough relevant multimodal problems.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two-stage data cleaning was performed: (1) Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were used to identify potential duplicate problems, which were then reviewed by authors to eliminate duplications. (2) Problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking, ensuring adherence to a standardized format. In a third stage, authors categorized problems into four difficulty levels (very easy, easy, medium, hard), and approximately 10% of problems classified as very easy were excluded from the benchmark.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MMMU is designed to monitor progress towards Expert AGI, defined as AI systems reaching "at least 90th percentile of skilled adults" in a broad range of tasks. Achieving Expert AGI could lead to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption. The benchmark aims to provide a rigorous standard for evaluating multimodal models and stimulate development of next-generation multimodal foundation models.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating multimodal foundation models on expert-level, college-level multi-discipline understanding and reasoning tasks. Benchmarking progress towards Expert AGI. Assessing models' perception, knowledge, and reasoning capabilities across diverse academic disciplines. Stimulating development of next-generation multimodal foundation models.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Annotators were instructed to avoid collecting questions that contain any private information. Data privacy compliance with privacy laws and ethical standards in data handling is described as paramount in the annotation protocol.
